Refutation-target: independent validation/review spawn on Grok still requires an active product xBRIEF because unmarked dest-cwd general-purpose with zero eligible briefs is #2885.

## Verdict

The mechanism half stands. Unmarked dest-cwd `general-purpose` at 0 eligible still fail-closes spawn with the missing-active text. I could not refute that for native `spawn_subagent`. The consequence half overstates "product xBRIEF" and folds a write problem into a spawn problem.

## 1. Dest-cwd cannot be the skip class

blocks-the-design

Evidence: `isProcessOnlyCriticSpawn` requires `plan` or `process_only`; dest-path is not a class (`packages/core/src/hooks/readonly.ts`). Fixture `does not skip on dest-path cwd without process_only` passed. Dispatcher recovery names dest-path as not that class. Pin at dispatch-sha f33b8b8e: do not skip #2885 on destProven.

Failure mode: binding issue Expected "spawn_subagent with dest worktrees" without a host-visible marker would skip #2885 on destProven and treat every dest-cwd general-purpose as validation.

Disposition: a bindable map must keep dest-path out of skip class. The marker stays host-visible (`process_only` or a new advertised field). Implement-class never sets it.

## 2. Spawn without xBRIEF and specs writes are different gates

sharpens-framing

Evidence: requirements posture (#4444) is `!isSpawnTool` then `write-requirements-ready`. Allow paths already include `specs/**`; deny includes `packages/**`, `src/**`, `cmd/**` (`packages/core/src/session/posture.ts`). Tests passed: allows docs/REQUIREMENTS.md after occupancy without ritual or scope; denies packages writes. Spawn tools never take that branch.

`process_only` spawn is `spawn-process-only-ready` with no dest occupancy and no leftover `file_scope`. Child writes still hit mutation gates. Assist-scratch is `.deft-scratch/` and `temp/`, not `specs/`.

Failure mode: binding a new `specs/**-validation-pass*` write class as the P1 remedy leaves native spawn denied. Binding process_only as the specs write allowlist lets spawn through and still denies tracked specs writes without occupancy plus requirements posture.

Disposition: state two clauses. P1 is writing-capable spawn without a passable skip-class field. Specs writes after occupancy already exist on requirements posture. Do not mint a second specs fence unless child occupancy and posture are named.

## 3. Native advertised spawn has no writing skip class

sharpens-framing

Evidence: this host's advertised `spawn_subagent` fields are prompt, description, subagent_type (`general-purpose` | `explore` | `plan`), background, isolation, resume_from, cwd, model. No `process_only`, no `worker_role`. Playbook: pass is the field on stdin; advertised JSON omitting it is an upstream schema ask. `explore` is spawn-explore-ready and read-only. `plan` is skip-class but cannot post (no Shell). Unmarked `general-purpose` at 0 eligible is #2885 (`dispatcher.ts` spawn-has-no-write-target comment; `scope.ts` missing-active message; `still denies spawn when no active scope even without a write target (#2885)` passed on the Cursor Task fixture). CLI `grok --cwd --prompt-file` is already classified process-only skip (#4219); that is not `spawn_subagent`.

Failure mode: a parallel skip-class in the hook, while the advertised JSON still cannot carry a marker, reprints #4315.

Disposition: name the passable field or keep CLI last-resort. Do not add dest-path skip to paper over the schema omit.

## 4. Eligible count is not product-shaped

sharpens-framing

Evidence: `inspectActiveScope` eligibles are preflight-passing active artifacts, not a product-shape predicate. 0 eligible → missing-active #2885. 1 eligible + dest cwd + parent id → implement-class dest-lock and leftover `file_scope`. 2+ → Deny 1. Recovery text already says do not invent a fake scope.

Failure mode: operators mint a dummy story to unlock spawn, then inherit dest-lock and fail `scope:complete` (#4421). A tree with one leftover running brief does not print P1's missing-active text.

Disposition: write "eligible active xBRIEF", not "product xBRIEF". Validation on leftover-active trees is dest-lock, not this P1.

## Injection / swarm

sharpens-framing

Spawn, dest worktrees, occupancy, and shared dest are in play.

- Prompt, free-text, and dest-path classification is already refused. Keep it refused.
- A new glob `specs/**-validation-pass*` as a classifier is weaker than the existing requirements fence (`specs/**` plus deny list plus symlink refuse). Path crafting belongs on that fence, not a second glob.
- N validators as implement-class dest-lock occupy dest and linger leftover `file_scope`. Skip-class shares dest cwd-without-occupy. Validation is the latter, or it is occupancy linger.
- Implement envelope signals already win over ephemeral markers. Keep that polarity.
- `isolation=worktree` plus cwd is invalid-extra-destination, not a hatch.

## Road not taken

Strongest rejected position: P1 is already shipped via process_only plus CLI last-resort plus requirements `specs/**` writes.

Steelman: `spawn-process-only-ready` at 0, 1, and many leftover is locked; CLI argv dest-present is the same skip; requirements writes skip ritual and story xBRIEF after occupancy.

What would flip: advertised `spawn_subagent` grows a writing skip-class field that operators can actually pass, and the child can take requirements posture with occupancy for `specs/**`. Until then the native writing spawn at 0 eligible stays #2885.

## Inventory (existing, not new)

- explore / plan advertised seats (read-only / no Shell)
- process_only stdin skip (#4296 / #4315)
- CLI last-resort grok --cwd (#4219 / #4391)
- ephemeral/docs/assist spawn (#3080 / #3259); Grok advertised schema has no worker_role
- session:start --read-only (occupancy/ritual, not spawn skip)
- requirements posture writes (#4444)
- assist-scratch `.deft-scratch/` `temp/` (#1802)
- CHANGELOG Unreleased at f33b8b8e: no validation-spawn recut

## Re-verification

Ran vitest at dispatch-sha f33b8b8e against this dest. Passed: unmarked spawn #2885 deny; dest-path is not skip class; process_only lander; requirements posture write tests. dest-proven Grok fixture file (`dispatcher-spawn-dest.test.ts`) had 21 failures on this host: dest classified destination-foreign (Windows worktree path) before the #2885 message. That is a fixture-env miss, not a recut of the source comment at `dispatcher.ts:1925`.

Closed #3080 / #3259 / #4444 remain other hosts/postures for spawn. They are not this Grok writing-spawn hole.

## footnote — P3 is downstream of P2 and should not buy a mechanism limb

`evaluateBoundedPrWatchDeny` refuses bare `pr:watch` without `--monitor-agent-id` when Tier 1 is provable. The Approach 1 one-liner always passes `--monitor-agent-id` (`review-monitor/verify.ts:364`). Once the spawn is admitted, the parent never reaches for parent-shell bare watch, so the stamp-clear carve-out never arises. P3 relieves as a consequence of P2 rather than as its own remedy limb. Census only; no disposition weight.

## footnote — the dest-cwd requirement is a residual, smaller tax

`processOnlyCriticRequiresDest` means the flag form still requires an existing linked dest worktree, so babysitting PRs #6161 / #6162 means creating a worktree at `origin/<default>` to watch branches it does not contain. Materially cheaper than create-promote-activate-preflight-complete, and #4296 dest-first is a deliberate prior decision, so this is not a reopen. Recorded so Bound does not claim zero ceremony.

## Road not taken

Treating this as a deny-text-only fix — relabel option (4), change nothing else. Rejected: the field note shows the text was visible and did not route the operator, and the emitting callers still produce no marker, so the operator would have to hand-assemble the payload. The relabel is necessary and not sufficient.

## Steelman for Approach B, and what would flip this

B's strongest case is precisely the two blocking findings above. A distinct `review_monitor` / `validation` class would let the deny route by role without overloading "critic", would let the dest and occupancy convention differ per class instead of forcing one flag to carry two, and would let a `drive-to: merge-ready` babysit be admitted under a class whose conflict predicate is tuned for it.

What flips my verdict to B: if the panel concludes the occupancy convention genuinely must diverge — shared no-occupy for monitors, per-seat occupied for writing validation seats — then one marker carrying two conventions is worse than two classes, and B's extra surface area is the honest price. My verdict rests on the judgment that the divergence is expressible as a dispatch-side dest rule rather than a second hook class. Show that it is not, and B wins.

## Lean

A, scoped down. Not A as drafted, and not B.

## Bound remedy

- Emit `process_only: true` plus dest `cwd` from the Approach 1 babysit spawn surface (`swarm/approach1-babysitter.ts` card, `review-monitor/verify.ts:357`) and from the validation-seat dispatch.
- Bind that emission to the `stop-at: pr-open` + `worker_role: review-monitor` shape only; never the `drive-to: merge-ready` variant.
- Relabel #2885 recovery option (4) (`dispatcher.ts:2456`) from "Process-only critic" to capability wording covering critic, review-monitor, and validation seats.
- When a process-only marker is present but suppressed by `hasImplementConflictSignal`, deny naming the suppressing field instead of the generic #2885 text.
- One dest per validation seat that writes a report root; keep shared cwd-without-occupy for seats that write nothing.
- Do not add a new spawn class, and do not widen `hasImplementConflictSignal`.

Leftover, out of Bound: report-root fence work (already covered by `REQUIREMENTS_DEFAULT_ALLOW_PATHS`), P3 bounded-watch (downstream of P2), dest-cwd residual (#4296 prior decision).

## Summary
Independent multi-agent **validation** (read product code, write only `specs/…-validation-pass*` artifacts, no product mutation) still cannot `spawn_subagent` on Grok Build **0.119.2** without inventing and activating a **product-shaped active xBRIEF**.

Deny text:
> No active xBRIEF artifact was found under xbrief/active/ … Recovery: scope:promote …

Closed work (#3080 ephemeral docs Task, #3259 local-dev without xBRIEF, #4444 requirements posture) does **not** cover this Grok path. Operators running `/phase-validate` must author a fake scope brief, promote, activate, then later fight `scope:complete` delivery evidence (#4421 class) for a docs-only pass.

## Why this is wrong for normal users
Validation is explicitly **not** implementation. Requiring a story xBRIEF to spawn independent reviewers:
- Adds 10–20 minutes of ceremony before any clause is checked
- Forces dummy `file_scope` / acceptance clauses
- Leaves active/completed lifecycle pollution for process work
- Trains agents to mint scopes just to unlock hooks

## Expected
A first-class posture or spawn class for **independent validation / review** that:
- Allows `spawn_subagent` with dest worktrees
- Allows writes under `specs/**-validation-pass*` (and similar allowlisted report roots)
- Does **not** require a product story xBRIEF
- Still fails closed on `apps/` `packages/` product paths

## Actual
Had to `xbrief:create` → edit → `scope:promote` → `scope:activate` → `xbrief:preflight` before any validator could launch; then could not `scope:complete` without a merge commit for this process brief.

## Environment
- Grok Build, macOS
- `@deftai/directive@0.119.2`
- Consumer `deftai/notetechnic` running skill `phase-validate` for M1-05..M1-08

## Related (not duplicates)
- Closed #3080 / #3259 / #4444 — different hosts/postures; gap remains on Grok validation spawn
- Open #4575 — dest recovery opacity (compounded this)
- Closed #4421 — complete-vs-merge chicken egg (hit when finishing the invented brief)
